messages:
isabel: Heads-up — I'm going to open a Terraform + k8s change for inference-api. Goal: move TLS termination to backend (TLS passthrough) so the service can do client mTLS. Will change Gateway binding + LB type to support TCP passthrough. Need quick checks on healthchecks, externalTrafficPolicy, and SG rules. PR soon: https://git.company/repo/pulls/987

samir: quick TLDR? why are we doing passthrough instead of letting ALB terminate?

isabel: TLDR: compliance requires client certificate verification at the app layer for this tenant. ALB termination drops client certs. Plan: switch the Gateway to use NLB/TargetGroup with protocol=TCP (passthrough), annotate the Service/gateway to pass raw TLS through. Also set externalTrafficPolicy=Local to preserve client IPs for auth + auditing. Terraform will adjust the aws_lb_target_group and listener to TCP 443 -> target group on nodeport.

maria: healthchecks: if we go TCP passthrough, do we need TCP healthchecks at the LB level and keep HTTP readiness probe on pods? any mismatch will make k8s think pod is ready but LB mark unhealthy.

isabel: good call. We'll set LB healthcheck to TCP (port 443) and keep k8s readinessProbe as HTTP on /ready (app handles TLS handshake once routed). The LB TCP check just verifies connection acceptance. Example k8s svc snippet I plan to apply:

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: inference-api
  annotations:
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-type: "nlb"
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-backend-protocol: "tcp"
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer
  externalTrafficPolicy: Local
  ports:
  - name: tls-443
    port: 443
    protocol: TCP
    targetPort: 8443
```

samir: session affinity? if TLS passthrough, sticky sessions might be needed for long-lived connections.

isabel: we'll avoid session affinity at LB; app uses token-based auth and the mTLS session is short. If we need sticky later we can enable NLB target group-level stickiness (session duration). For now externalTrafficPolicy:Local + NodePort ensures client IPs and preserves source.

ethan: security groups/nodes: will the terraform change open 443 across all nodes? that's a blast radius. we should scope SG to the NLB and only allow the ALB->NLB flow or client IPs where appropriate.

isabel: planned SG change: create sg "inference-nlb" attached to NLB with inbound 443 from 0.0.0.0/0 (public) and outbound to node SG on 8443 only. In k8s nodes, we restrict node SG to accept 8443 only from NLB SG. Terraform snippet I'll include in PR:

```hcl
resource "aws_lb" "inference_nlb" {
  name               = "inference-nlb"
  internal           = false
  load_balancer_type = "network"
  subnets            = var.public_subnets
}
resource "aws_security_group_rule" "nlb_to_nodes" {
  type                     = "egress"
  from_port                = 8443
  to_port                  = 8443
  protocol                 = "tcp"
  security_group_id        = aws_security_group.nlb_sg.id
  cidr_blocks              = [aws_security_group.node_sg.id] # pseudo, we'll use a data lookup
}
```

ops-bot: terraform fmt OK on branch 987-change-nlb-passthrough (auto-check) :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: terraform plan shows LB -> TG protocol change, no terraform drift for k8s resources.

tess: rollout plan? I'd rather a canary than flip everything at once.

isabel: agreed. Canary plan: create inference-api-canary service + deployment (same image), attach a Gateway route with weight 10 to canary. Smoke test with cert/key from staging tenant. Steps:
- apply canary svc (same manifest with name inference-api-canary)
- update Gateway HTTPRoute/TCPRoute (Gateway API) weights: canary 10, primary 90
- run smoke script: ./scripts/smoke-mtls --host inference.canary.redwood.test --cert test-client.pem
If smoke passes for 24h, increase to 50 then flip. I'll include kubectl commands in PR.

maria: pinging @samir @ethan for review on healthcheck/SG parts.

isabel: PR opened: https://git.company/repo/pulls/987 - requesting reviews from @samir @ethan @tess. Will wait 24h for comments, then coordinate a 2-hour maintenance window for the canary deploy. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
